parcalar.metin: [excited, emphatic science storyteller] The water held behind a dam is basically a giant battery! Energy Sources, episode three: water.
This energy also comes from the sun. The sun evaporates water, clouds drop rain and snow on the mountains, and rivers flow downhill.
A dam blocks the river and water piles up high. The higher the water falls from, the more energy it carries.
The water rushes down huge pipes called penstocks and slams into the turbine.
The turbine blades spin; a generator on the same shaft turns that rotation into electricity.
Transformers step up the voltage and power flows into the grid. Turkey's largest dam, the Atatürk Dam, has an installed capacity of two thousand four hundred megawatts.
Some plants pump water up to a higher lake when electricity is plentiful, and release it when it's needed. A true giant battery!
The world's largest is China's Three Gorges Dam, with more than twenty-two thousand megawatts of installed capacity.
[excited] From rain to electricity! Next episode: the power of the atom. Follow Kozmos Lab.
